# Best portable power station for camping

The right pick depends on trip length and what you plan to power.

## Weekend tent or car camping (phones, lights, camera, CPAP)
The 250-500Wh class is the sweet spot, since it's light enough to carry one-handed.

- **Bluetti Elite 30 V2** (288Wh, 600W): TechRadar's budget pick. It lists at $289.99, and Dealectric's tested code **AFF5OFF** brings it to about $275.50 as of 2026-10-25. [Buy at Bluetti via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-30-v2). Dealectric earns a commission on purchases through that link, and the checkout has the final word on price.
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (288Wh, 8.3 lb, ~$249): PowerStationGearLab's top camping pick. Jackery has replaced it with the 300 v2, but the Plus is still sold through Amazon and others. [Details and price link](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (288Wh, ~$199): It has a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Confirm you're buying the standard AC-outlet model, not the AC-less "C300 DC". [Details](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (286Wh, 600W, ~$269-299): It can expand to 572Wh. [Details](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

Note that OutdoorGearLab's lab tests scored the Jackery Explorer 300 (52) and Anker C300 (50) fairly low overall. They still named the Jackery 300 its best buy for phones and laptops. If you want to run more than small electronics, step up in size. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)

## Multi-day trips, electric cooler or fridge, van camping
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2**: OutdoorGearLab's best for off-grid camping. It has 2,200W output, weighs 39 lb, and was recently under $900 on Amazon. [Review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (1,070Wh, ~$799): TechRadar's best for camping. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2**: OutdoorGearLab's best value, on sale under $530. It has a noisy fan and a smaller usable capacity (890Wh measured). [Review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra**: WIRED's best for camping at about $1,079. It's IP65-rated, weighs just under 40 lb, and has a 5-year warranty. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

## Quick tips
- A phone charge takes about 10Wh, and a CPAP about 30-60Wh per night with the humidifier off.
- A folding solar panel lets you recharge in the field.
- These units are too large for airplanes, so they're for car or campsite use.

I didn't get direct purchase URLs for the Jackery, Anker, or EcoFlow models in the results, so those links go to the review pages that list them. Tell me your trip length and what you'll run, and I can narrow it to one pick.
